title: Audit backcompat guidance — concise v0p1
content:
Purpose:
A short working note to capture an opinionated, operationally pragmatic approach for audit/event schema backward compatibility, cross-version event taxonomy alignment, and a minimal SIEM shim for evidence handoff. Focus: reduce developer churn during schema changes, keep SIEM ingestion stable, and enable incremental evidence automation without a big-bang migration.

Context / motivation:
- We have multiple consumers of events: internal consoles, SIEM (Splunk/Elastic), forensic export tools, Dedicated/Private runtime collectors, and downstream evidence automation pipelines.
- Recent schema changes (v1->v2) caused some consumers to drop optional fields; v2->v3 introduced event_type splitting that broke rule-based SIEM parsers.
- Goal is to define a small, testable surface that keeps old consumers working while allowing schema evolution.

Definitions (short):
- canonical-event: the latest agreed wire representation (vN) used internally and in new exports.
- stable-hint: a small set of top-level fields guaranteed to remain readable across versions (event_id, timestamp, event_family, provenance, severity, actor.id, resource.id).
- shim-envelope: a lightweight wrapper produced by the audit bridge to present legacy view for older consumers or SIEM parsers.

Core principles:
1) Contract minimalism: keep a compact stable-hint; everything else may vary. Consumers must prefer stable-hint for routing and critical controls.
2) Schema layering: produce canonical-event + shim-envelope on write for 18 months after major change.
3) Idempotent backfills: backfill jobs must be safe to run repeatedly and mark progress via ledger.
4) Observability-first: each schema change ships with compatibility tests, a traced rollout, and a SIEM parser regression suite.

Event naming and taxonomy rules (practical):
- event_family is required and coarse-grained (e.g., auth, config, data_plane, billing, admin). This is the primary SIEM grouping.
- event_type can be hierarchical with slashes: auth.login.success, auth.login.failure, auth.token.rotate. Avoid ad-hoc synonyms.
- When splitting an event_type into two (v -> v+1), keep the old event_type name present as a compat alias inside shim-envelope.compat_names array for 12 months.
- Use semantic version tag in event metadata: event_schema: "audit.v3". This is machine-checkable by the bridge.

Shim-envelope design (minimal):
- Top-level shim fields (always present): shim_version, shim_timestamp, canonical_ref (id + schema), compat_names (list), stable_hints (object).
- Example shim (textual):
  shim_version: "shim.v1"
  shim_timestamp: "2026-02-01T13:04:00Z"
  canonical_ref: { id: "evt-12345", schema: "audit.v3" }
  compat_names: ["login_success", "user_login_ok"]
  stable_hints: { event_id: "evt-12345", timestamp: "2026-02-01T13:03:59Z", event_family: "auth", actor_id: "user:982" }
- The shim envelope should be compact and easily parsed by existing SIEM line-parsers (i.e., few nested structures, mostly strings).

Backfill / rollforward strategy (v1->v3 path):
- Phase 0: schema freeze + announce (2 weeks). Publish changelog and compatibility table.
- Phase 1: bridge implementation: audit-producer writes canonical-event (v3) AND shim-envelope (shim.v1) concurrently. New consumers read canonical-event; legacy consumers read shim. (duration: 6 weeks)
- Phase 2: soft-checks: enable SIEM ingest of shim for production traffic with sampling 5%->50% while monitoring parser errors. (duration: 4 weeks)
- Phase 3: scheduled backfill: for historical records, run idempotent backfill that reads archived events and emits shim-envelope variants into the SIEM staging index. Track progress in ledger: BACKFILL.AUDIT.LAST_TS.
- Phase 4: deprecation: after 12–18 months and when parser error-rate < 0.1% and client opt-in rate low, retire shim and stop producing compat_names.

RBAC v2 interplay notes:
- RBAC events must include minimal auth visibility in stable_hints: actor.id, actor.role_snapshot (string), resource.id, action. Do not embed full policy documents inside events — instead provide policy_id and a delta-ref for debugging.
- When RBAC role semantics change, emit a delta event: rbac.role.rotate with role_diff_url (signed short-lived URL) so evidence automation can fetch older role version if needed.
- Ensure PII and token material are never present in shim-envelope fields. If redaction occurs, annotate stable_hints.redaction = "partial|full".

Evidence automation & SIEM export considerations:
- Evidence automation consumers may require richer payloads (full request/response traces, K/V cache refs). Those can be exposed via canonical_event.attachments with pointer references to evidence store. Attachments must be referenced by content-hash and KMS-signed locator.
- For SIEM export, prefer a flattened export index derived from shim-envelope.stable_hints to keep rules simple. Keep heavy payloads out of SIEM and link to evidence in a separate forensic bucket.
- Export rate-throttling: SIEM connectors should sample large-volume noisy events (e.g., telemetry.ping) and send aggregate metrics instead of individual events. Document sampling policy per event_family.

Compatibility test checklist (automated):
- unit: serializer round-trip for canonical_event and shim-envelope for each topology change.
- integration: ingest shim into staging SIEM parser and assert no parse-errors for 99.9% of sampled traffic.
- e2e: evidence automation consumers can fetch pointer references from canonical_event.attachments and validate signatures.

Operational runbook snippets (to include in ops-oncall playbooks):
- If SIEM parser error spike > 1%: switch SIEM to fallback index and enable debug capture for 10% of traffic. Notify schema-leads.
- If backfill backlog grows > 72h: pause new backfills, scale the backfill workers, and mark the ledger with a pause token.

Unresolved / open questions:
- What is cross-tenant privacy policy for storing attachments referenced by canonical_event? (need legal + privacy input)
- Should shim generation be implemented in producer SDKs or centralized bridge service? Tradeoffs: latency vs uniformity.
- Long-term retention for shim envelopes vs canonical events: align with retention policy but avoid double-billing storage.

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- Sofia: draft Confluence page with changelog matrix and announce timeline (due 2026-02-05).
- Evan: prototype shim-envelope serializer in producer SDK and PR to repo (GITHUB:repo/audit-schema#45) (due 2026-02-12).
- Priya: draft SIEM parser regression suite and sample dataset (due 2026-02-08).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a compact numeric event_family code to help tiny devices with bandwidth constraints.
- Explore signed compact diffs for RBAC role snapshots (instead of full role fetch).

References and quick links:
- JIRA:SEC-1987 (schema change request)
- CONFLUENCE:SEC-AUDIT-TAX-2026 (taxonomy draft)
- GITHUB:repo/audit-schema#45 (shim PoC)
short_summary: Operational plan for shipping a shim-envelope for audit schema backcompat, taxonomy rules, RBAC v2 interactions, SIEM export guidance, and idempotent backfill/retirement timeline.
